tasks.language_instruction: Grasp the handle and open the hinged door by at least 60 degrees.

tasks.language_instruction: Turn the valve counterclockwise by 90 degrees relative to its initial angle.
tasks.novelty: Unlike Base 36–47/56 gear insertion, 52 bulb insertion, and 53 bolt/nut mating, this transfers torque into a passive single-axis valve without insertion or thread engagement.

tasks.language_instruction: Press the spring button at least 8 mm for 0.3 seconds, then release it.
tasks.novelty: None of the original 76 tasks requires a displacement-dependent restoring force and measured press–hold–release sequence; connector contact alone cannot satisfy this task.

tasks.language_instruction: Move the bistable lever from the negative well to the positive well, then let go.
tasks.novelty: Unlike Base 12–23 key insertion or 53 bolt/nut mating, this crosses a conservative bistable barrier and must retain the new state after robot release.

tasks.language_instruction: Pull the cap completely out of its spring-loaded retaining shoes and move it away by at least 3 cm.
tasks.novelty: Unlike Blind 3/7 free ribbed-cap selection/transport and Base/Dynamic insertion, this cap starts captured between spring-loaded retaining shoes and must physically overcome their friction.

episode_config.physics_timestep_note: 400 Hz resolves the passive 4000 N/m retaining shoes; 100 Hz produced sustained reset angular-speed oscillation. Mechanical parameters and 20 Hz control unchanged.

tasks.language_instruction: Follow the thin sinusoidal rail from its left end to its right end while maintaining tactile contact.
tasks.novelty: Unlike Blind 1/3–7 texture selection and Base 49 search, this measures ordered coverage and continuous gel contact along a known rigid contour, not object identity or terminal location.

tasks.language_instruction: Pivot the block upright by 90 degrees while keeping it supported by the table and allowing rotation within the gripper.
tasks.novelty: Unlike Base 48 lift-and-insert peg reorientation, this requires continuous tabletop support and at least 60 degrees of object rotation relative to the hand; lifting and replacing is rejected.
tasks.physical_design: A visible narrow 30 mm tabletop support provides clearance for the unmodified GSmini housings; support contact is measured against this fixed table-mounted support.

tasks.novelty: Unlike Base pick-and-insert and Extra 6 fixed-rail tracing, the movable block itself must traverse an ordered 160 mm S curve under sustained gel and tabletop contact. Lifting and carrying cannot satisfy the history.

tasks.physical_design: A 50 mm diameter, 50 mm tall rigid balsa push block has a round face represented by 128 radial facets. Closed mesh volume at manufacturer reference density 150 kg/m3 gives mass 0.014720302298225406 kg and uniform-density inertia. At the 25 mm contact height, nominal static breakaway is below 0.08 N and steady sliding drag remains above 0.06 N even at maximum upward gel shear. Friction, gravity, success criteria and GSmini remain fixed. Bamboo PBR is an engineering wood appearance.

tasks.language_instruction: Roll the can through half a turn along the table without sliding or lifting it.
tasks.novelty: Tactile Gym includes object rolling. This benchmark adapts that family to a cylindrical can: translation must match radius times the unwrapped rolling angle with limited slip, unlike Base ball sorting or Extra 7 supported pivoting.

tasks.physical_design: A hollow polypropylene cup with raised bail and integral grip rails. Actual material volume at 900 kg/m3 determines mass and inertia. The robot must thread the open handle, transfer weight to the fixed steel hook and release without housing support.

tasks.language_instruction: Lift the rod, hold the hand still, allow a twenty millimeter downward slip, then tighten the fingers to arrest it without regrasping.
tasks.novelty: Real tactile manipulation studies detect slip and tighten or recover grasps. This task measures deliberate gravity-driven axial translation followed by arrest, distinct from identity selection, insertion, or object reorientation; hand motion, housing support, cross-axis tilt and dropped regrasping are rejected. Axial yaw is recorded without imposing an orientation target.

reset_contract.grip_reference: Locked only after a stable two-gel grasp is lifted at least 30 mm above the table. Initial approach and pickup do not count as axial slip.

tasks.physical_design: A vertical, constant-section balsa rod must slide downward under gravity and then stop. Cross-axis tilt beyond two degrees is rejected. Axial yaw is diagnostic; the final angular-speed limit applies to all axes.

tasks.language_instruction: Pick up the horizontal rod near its center, orient it upright, place its flat end beside the cradle, then release and retreat while it stands unsupported.
tasks.novelty: Free-standing placement after unsupported pickup and 90-degree reorientation. Unlike Base 48/55 there is no socket; unlike Extra 7 the robot releases the object; unlike Extra 14 there is no deliberate axial slide.

reset_contract.support_geometry: Native tabletop ray plus actual source collision radius and authored V face planes; no random Z.

tasks.physical_design: Use the shared 6.048 g balsa rod and its flat end caps for standing placement. Mass and inertia follow actual material volume at 150 kg/m3. A fixed V cradle leaves the center clear for pickup. Native history must show unsupported pickup, reorientation, end-cap seating and release without an attachment, socket or side prop.

tasks.language_instruction: Grasp the raised latch grip, depress its spring-loaded lug below the keeper, slide it clear along the rail, then release and retreat while the plunger returns.
tasks.novelty: Two coupled passive translations with a real collision interlock. Unlike Extra 0 or 3, a press alone or a slide alone cannot clear the keeper. No software unlock, attachment or target drive.

reset_contract.support_geometry: Native tabletop ray plus authored collision base bottom z=0; common SE(2) jitter, no random Z.

tasks.physical_design: Independent low-load latch with a solid PA12 plunger: 14.09152 g from collision-solid union volume and manufacturer typical density 1010 kg/m3. Native gel end faces depress and translate the cap; housing support is forbidden. Collision boxes, passive bearings, keeper and fixed 0.15 N spring preload are unchanged. Engineering material selection, not hardware calibration.

tasks.language_instruction: Briefly touch each of the three inspection coupons, lifting clear between probes. Then indicate the raised defect with a steady final gel contact.
tasks.novelty: Discrete front-surface inspection with seeded defect position and a committed terminal answer. Unlike Extra 6, no continuous prescribed contour is traced.

reset_contract.support_geometry: Per-coupon native tabletop ray plus collision base bottom z=0; common SE(2) jitter and seeded permutation of the three slots.

tasks.physical_design: Three bolted bench fixtures; two flat plates and one 1.5 mm rounded raised boss. Kinematic mounting is fixture support, not attachment of a manipulated object. No material deformation, fracture or micron-scale metrology claim.

tasks.language_instruction: Withdraw the RAM module at least 2 cm, reinsert its keyed edge, then release it and retreat.
tasks.novelty: Keyed long-board withdrawal, reinsertion and released socket support; a final seated pose alone cannot succeed.

tasks.physical_design: Rigid keyed RAM insertion specimen with two visible 0.8 mm TPU grip strips on its heat spreader, mounted on a real fixed pedestal. Added mass uses manufacturer areal weight.
